server.name: rapidworkers
server.title: RapidWorkers
server.instructions:
RapidWorkers hires real people for paid microtasks (social engagement, reviews, sign-ups, app testing), surveys and AI data collection (photos, audio, video, text), paid in USD from the account balance. Rules: pay at least $0.05 per worker ($0.10 for AI tasks, $0.50 per survey response), at least 10 workers per job, $20 minimum deposit. Always call preview_job_cost before any create tool and confirm the total with the user before spending money.

Workflow: get_account (balance, deposit status) -> get_platform_info (categories, sub-category codes, prefilled job types, survey builder options, country codes) -> preview_job_cost -> show the total and wait for an explicit yes -> create_job, create_prefilled_job, create_survey or create_ai_task with the quote_id, confirm=true and a new idempotency_key -> list_jobs / get_job -> list_submissions -> approve_submission or reject_submission.

Money moves on create, extend, cancel (a $0.20 fee on live jobs), approve and tip. Approving pays the worker and cannot be undone, so check each proof against the job instructions first; rejection reasons must say exactly what was missing. Pending submissions are approved automatically after 2 days. If a call that moves money times out, retry it with the same idempotency_key so it is never done twice; after an error answer, fix the cause and use a new key.

A first deposit is required before posting, and earned balance cannot pay for jobs. get_deposit_link returns a checkout URL for the user to open and pay; never pay or enter card details yourself. New jobs can wait for a short moderation review (status pending_review) before going live. AI tasks need access approved by the RapidWorkers team (request_ai_task_access); surveys need none.

Surveys: create_survey builds a questionnaire workers answer on RapidWorkers (choice, rating, NPS, matrix, ranking, text, number and date questions, screening questions, show_if logic and attention checks). Use kind "survey" with preview_job_cost, list_jobs, get_job, extend_job, cancel_job and the review tools. list_submissions returns each response with its answers and a quality score and band; get_survey_results gives the per-question totals. Screened-out workers are not paid, and responses that failed the automatic checks arrive already rejected.

Every create tool takes an optional image_prompt: a detailed description of one image we generate with AI and show workers with the instructions. Write it from the job details; if you do not know what the image should show, ask the user before creating.

When the user refers to a job without its id ("that job", "the last one"), find it with list_jobs (newest first) and tell the user the job_id, title and creation time you are using; if more than one could match (for example several jobs with the same title), ask. list_submissions and get_job name the job they read, so check it is the one meant.

Errors come back as tool results with isError and say how to fix the call.

tools.name: get_account
tools.title: Get account
tools.description: Returns the account balance (USD), whether the account has made a deposit (required before posting jobs), AI task access status and the commission rate added to job costs.

tools.name: get_platform_info
tools.title: Get platform rules and options
tools.description: Returns platform rules (minimum pay $0.05 per task, $0.10 for AI tasks, $0.50 per survey response, at least 10 workers per job, $20 minimum deposit, commission and fees), job categories with sub-category codes, the prefilled job types with the link each one expects, AI task types, the survey builder options (question types, scale presets, attention check templates, limits and audience codes) and the allowed ISO country codes. Call it before creating a job or survey.

section.description: Return only one part: limits (pay, quantity, deposit, fees), categories (with sub-category codes), prefilled_job_types, ai_task_types, survey_builder (question types, scale presets, attention check templates, survey limits and audience codes) or countries. Default all.

tools.name: list_transactions
tools.title: List transactions
tools.description: Returns the 20 most recent balance transactions (deposits, job charges, refunds).

tools.name: get_deposit_link
tools.title: Create deposit link
tools.description: Creates a hosted checkout page and returns its URL for the account owner to open and pay. It does not charge anything by itself. Minimum $20. method "card" (Stripe; a 4% processing fee is deducted from the credited amount) or "crypto". The balance is credited only after payment completes; check get_account afterwards.

amount.description: Amount in USD to deposit, at least 20.00, at most 2 decimals.

method.description: "card" (Stripe checkout; a 4% processing fee is deducted from the credited amount) or "crypto" (crypto invoice).

tools.name: preview_job_cost
tools.title: Preview job cost
tools.description: Calculates the exact charge for a job, survey or AI task before creating it: pay rate x quantity + commission (+ $10 if a regular job is pinned), whether the balance covers it, and a quote_id valid for 10 minutes. Every create tool requires this quote_id, so call this first with the kind you will create ("job", "survey" or "ai_task") and show the total to the user. Rules: pay_rate >= 0.05 (>= 0.10 for kind "ai_task", >= 0.50 for kind "survey"), quantity >= 10 (at most 20,000 for AI tasks and surveys), pin only for kind "job".

kind.description: "job" (default) for regular and prefilled jobs, "survey" for surveys made with create_survey, "ai_task" for AI data-collection tasks.

pay_rate.description: USD paid to each worker, at most 2 decimals. At least 0.05 (0.10 for AI tasks, 0.50 for surveys).

quantity.description: Number of workers (one submission each). At least 10; AI tasks and surveys at most 20,000.

pin.description: Regular jobs only: pin the job to the top of the job list for $10. Default false.

tools.name: create_job
tools.title: Create job
tools.description: Posts a custom job that real workers complete and prove with a screenshot or text. Charges pay_rate x quantity + commission from the balance immediately. Requires quote_id from preview_job_cost, confirm=true after the user approved the total, and an idempotency_key (a new unique string; reuse it only to retry after a timeout). pay_rate >= 0.05 in every category, quantity >= 10. New jobs may be held for a short moderation review before going live. Optional image_prompt: a detailed description of one image we generate with AI and show workers on the job page.

title.description: Short title workers see in the job list (up to 200 characters).

description.description: Step-by-step instructions for the worker: what to do, where, and any rules. Plain text: put each step on its own line starting with "1.", "2." (or "-" for bullets); workers see them as a list and web addresses as links. HTML tags are not needed.

proof_required.description: What the worker must submit as proof, e.g. "Screenshot of your comment showing your username".

category.description: Category name from get_platform_info, e.g. "Social Media".

sub_category.description: Sub-category code from get_platform_info within that category, e.g. "2301".

pay_rate.description: USD paid to each worker, at most 2 decimals. At least 0.05 (0.10 for AI tasks, 0.50 for surveys).

quantity.description: Number of workers (one submission each). At least 10; AI tasks and surveys at most 20,000.

length_in_minutes.description: Honest estimate of the minutes one worker needs to finish the task.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes of the countries workers must be in, e.g. ["US", "GB"], or ["All"] for every country. get_platform_info lists the allowed codes.

excluded_countries.description: Only with countries ["All"] (or omitted): country codes to leave out.

pin.description: Pin the job to the top of the job list for $10 (must match the quote). Default false.

approve_once_full.description: true approves and pays every submission automatically once all slots are filled, without review. Default false: review them with list_submissions (unreviewed ones are approved after 2 days).

image_prompt.description: Optional, recommended when a picture would help workers. Describe ONE image we generate with AI (no extra cost) and show workers next to the instructions; it appears a minute or two after creation. We expand your description into a full design brief using the job details, so focus on intent and specifics: what the image is for (e.g. an example of a correct submission), photo or illustration, the exact layout and count (a grid of 2, 3, 4, 6 or 9 works best), what each part shows, and any exact text in quotes (a title, short labels). Example: "Photorealistic 3x3 grid of the same adult from nine angles (front, left 45, right 45, left profile, right profile, looking up, looking down, tilt left, tilt right), plain light background, a label under each photo, title "Required face angles"". If you do not know what the image should show (the product, page or expected result), ask the user before creating. Leave out if no image is wanted.

quote_id.description: quote_id from preview_job_cost for exactly this kind, pay rate, quantity and pin. Valid for 10 minutes.

confirm.description: Must be true, and only after the user explicitly approved this action and its cost.

idempotency_key.description: A new unique string for this action (e.g. a UUID; letters, digits, _ . : - only, up to 128). Send the same key again only to retry a call that timed out or could not reach the API, so it is never done twice. After an error answer, fix the cause and use a new key: the API replays its stored answer to a reused key.

tools.name: create_survey
tools.title: Create survey
tools.description: Posts a survey that real workers answer on RapidWorkers, built from your questions (choice, dropdown, rating with stars, agree scales or NPS, matrix, ranking, text, number, date, consent, text blocks and attention checks), and charges pay_rate x quantity + commission. No extra access is needed. Requires quote_id from preview_job_cost with kind "survey", confirm=true and an idempotency_key. pay_rate >= 0.50 per response, quantity 10 to 20,000, countries required. Questions are keyed q_1, q_2, ... by position (text blocks count): show_if may only point at an earlier question. Up to 5 screening questions must come first; screened-out workers are not paid and free their slot. Add 1 attention check (2 for surveys over 5 minutes). Every response gets a quality score; failed attention checks, impossible speed and repeat devices are rejected automatically. Optional image_prompt: one image we generate with AI and show workers with the survey intro.

title.description: Short title workers see in the survey list (up to 200 characters).

description.description: Intro workers read before they start: what the survey is about and anything they should know. Plain text (up to 5,000 characters), each paragraph on its own line. Say nothing about which answers screen people out.

type.description: single_choice (pick one), multiple_choice (pick several), dropdown (pick one from a long list), rating (one scale), matrix (several statements on one scale), ranking (order every option), short_text, long_text, number, date, consent (agree to a statement), statement (a text block, no answer) or attention_check (a platform check with its own wording).

label.description: The question as workers see it, plain text (up to 500 characters). Required except for attention_check. statement: the heading; consent: what the worker agrees to.

help_text.description: Optional note under the question (up to 1,000 characters); for a statement, its body text.

required.description: Whether an answer is needed (default true). Screening questions and attention checks are always required.

options.description: single_choice and multiple_choice: 2 to 20 choices; dropdown: 2 to 100; ranking: 2 to 10 items to put in order. Unique texts up to 200 characters. Leave "Other" and "None of the above" out: use allow_other and none_option.

allow_other.description: single_choice and multiple_choice: add "Other (please specify)" with a write-in box.

none_option.description: multiple_choice: text of an exclusive choice that clears the others, e.g. "None of the above".

randomize_options.description: single_choice, multiple_choice and ranking: shuffle the options for each worker (Other and None stay last), against order bias in unordered lists.

min_choices.description: multiple_choice: fewest choices a worker must tick.

max_choices.description: multiple_choice: most choices a worker may tick.

preset.description: stars_5 (1-5 stars), agree_5 (1 strongly disagree to 5 strongly agree), agree_7 (1-7), nps (0-10, rating only) or custom (set min, max and the end labels).

min.description: custom only: the first point, 0 or 1.

max.description: custom only: the last point; 2 to 11 points in all (a matrix 2 to 7).

min_label.description: custom only: text at the low end, e.g. "Not at all".

max_label.description: custom only: text at the high end, e.g. "Very much".

scale.description: rating and matrix: the answer scale. Default stars_5 for rating, agree_5 for matrix.

rows.description: matrix: 2 to 10 statements, each rated on the shared scale.

max_length.description: short_text (up to 500, default 500) and long_text (up to 10,000, default 2,000): most characters.

show_if.description: Show this item only when every condition holds (up to 3). Not on screening questions or attention checks. Hidden questions are skipped and never required.

question.description: Key of an EARLIER single_choice, multiple_choice, dropdown, rating, number, text, date or consent question, e.g. "q_2".

operator.description: single_choice and dropdown: is, is_not; multiple_choice: includes, excludes; rating and number: eq, gte, lte; any of them: answered, not_answered.

value.description: is, is_not, includes, excludes: the exact option text (or "other", or the none_option text). eq, gte, lte: a number written as text, e.g. "7". Leave out for answered and not_answered.

screener.description: Screening question (single_choice, multiple_choice or dropdown; up to 5, all before any other question). A worker who picks a disqualify answer leaves the survey unpaid, without a rejection, and the slot reopens.

disqualify.description: Screening questions only: the exact option texts that screen a worker out (at least one option must let them continue). Never shown to workers.

page_break_before.description: Start a new page at this item. A page break always follows the screening questions.

template.description: attention_check only: select_option (pick the named colour), agree_scale (pick the named agreement level) or nonsense_statement (disagree with an absurd statement). The platform writes the wording and the right answer for each worker.

questions.description: The survey items in order: 1 to 60, at most 50 that take an answer. Their keys are q_1, q_2, ... by position (text blocks count); show_if refers to them. Example: [{"type":"single_choice","label":"Do you drive a car at least once a week?","options":["Yes","No"],"screener":true,"disqualify":["No"]},{"type":"rating","label":"How likely are you to recommend your car brand to a friend?","scale":{"preset":"nps"}},{"type":"long_text","label":"What would make you more likely to recommend it?","show_if":[{"question":"q_2","operator":"lte","value":"6"}]},{"type":"attention_check","template":"select_option"}]

pay_rate.description: USD paid for each completed response, at least 0.50, at most 2 decimals. Workers see the effective hourly pay (pay_rate x 60 / minutes).

quantity.description: Number of responses wanted (one per worker), 10 to 20,000.

length_in_minutes.description: Optional: honest minutes one response takes. Leave out for our estimate from the questions (about 8 seconds per closed question, 30 per short text and 60 per long text answer).

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes of the countries workers must be in, e.g. ["US", "GB"], or ["All"] for every country. get_platform_info lists the allowed codes. Required for surveys.

excluded_countries.description: Only with countries ["All"] (or omitted): country codes to leave out.

genders.description: Only workers whose profile gender is one of these.

native_languages.description: Only workers with one of these native languages: codes such as "en", "es" or "hi" (get_platform_info section survey_builder lists them).

education.description: Only workers whose profile highest education is one of these.

occupations.description: Only workers whose profile occupation is one of these.

audience.description: Optional: who may answer, on top of countries. Leave out for everyone. Only workers with a completed profile match a filter, so every filter shrinks the pool: set only what the user asked for.

block_paste.description: true stops workers pasting into text answers, so they must type them. Default false; pasted answers are flagged either way.

image_prompt.description: Optional, recommended when a picture would help workers. Describe ONE image we generate with AI (no extra cost) and show workers next to the instructions; it appears a minute or two after creation. We expand your description into a full design brief using the job details, so focus on intent and specifics: what the image is for (e.g. an example of a correct submission), photo or illustration, the exact layout and count (a grid of 2, 3, 4, 6 or 9 works best), what each part shows, and any exact text in quotes (a title, short labels). Example: "Photorealistic 3x3 grid of the same adult from nine angles (front, left 45, right 45, left profile, right profile, looking up, looking down, tilt left, tilt right), plain light background, a label under each photo, title "Required face angles"". If you do not know what the image should show (the product, page or expected result), ask the user before creating. Leave out if no image is wanted.

idempotency_key.description: A new unique string for this action (e.g. a UUID; letters, digits, _ . : - only, up to 128). Send the same key again only to retry a call that timed out or could not reach the API, so it is never done twice. After an error answer, fix the cause and use a new key: the API replays its stored answer to a reused key.

required_file_count.description: Files each worker uploads (1 to 200). Required for image, video and audio collection; ignored otherwise.

capture_mode.description: Audio and video only: "upload" files, "record" in the browser, or "both" (default).

tools.name: request_ai_task_access
tools.title: Request AI task access
tools.description: Sends a request to enable AI data-collection tasks for this account, or returns the current status. An admin reviews requests; until approved, create_ai_task fails.

note.description: Optional: what data you plan to collect, so the team can approve faster.

Set kind to "survey" for surveys made with create_survey or "ai_task" for AI data-collection tasks; the default "job" covers regular and prefilled jobs.

kind.description: "job" (default) for regular and prefilled jobs, "survey" for surveys made with create_survey, "ai_task" for AI data-collection tasks.

search.description: Regular jobs only: text to find in the title or description.

tools.title: Get job
tools.description: Returns one job, survey or AI task by id with its brief, pay, targeting and progress; for a survey also its questions (keys q_1, q_2, ... with option ids), audience, response counts and quality bands. Set kind to "survey" for surveys made with create_survey or "ai_task" for AI data-collection tasks; the default "job" covers regular and prefilled jobs.

job_id.description: Id of the job, survey or AI task (job_id from list_jobs or from the create tool).

kind.description: "job" (default) for regular and prefilled jobs, "survey" for surveys made with create_survey, "ai_task" for AI data-collection tasks.

Set kind to "survey" for surveys made with create_survey or "ai_task" for AI data-collection tasks; the default "job" covers regular and prefilled jobs.

tools.title: Cancel job

Pending (not yet live) jobs are refunded in full; live jobs pay a $0.20 fee and cannot be canceled while submissions await review. Requires confirm=true. Set kind to "survey" for surveys made with create_survey or "ai_task" for AI data-collection tasks; the default "job" covers regular and prefilled jobs.

tools.name: list_submissions
tools.title: List submissions
tools.description: Lists submissions for a job, newest first, filtered by status (Pending, Approved, Rejected). Each has the proof text, proof image links and the worker's approval rate. For kind "survey" each response has its answers (question key, label and the answer as text), a quality score (0-100), a quality band (good, check, likely_bad) with the flags behind it, and whether it was rejected automatically; quality_band filters by band. Paginated with page and page_size (max 100). Pending submissions are approved automatically after 2 days if not reviewed. Set kind to "survey" for surveys made with create_survey or "ai_task" for AI data-collection tasks; the default "job" covers regular and prefilled jobs.

status.description: Only submissions with this status, e.g. "Pending" to review.

quality_band.description: Surveys only: only responses in this quality band, e.g. "likely_bad" to check the weakest first.

tools.name: get_survey_results
tools.title: Get survey results
tools.description: Returns the aggregated results of a survey (job_id from create_survey or list_jobs with kind "survey"): the response funnel (started, screened out, submitted, pending, approved, rejected), median time and effective hourly pay, quality bands, and per question the answer counts and percentages, means and medians, the NPS score, rankings, number ranges and the latest text answers. include "valid" (default: pending and approved responses), "approved" or "all" (adds rejected); screened-out workers never count. For each response in full use list_submissions with kind "survey".

job_id.description: Id of the survey (job_id from create_survey, or list_jobs with kind "survey").

include.description: Which responses count: "valid" (default) pending and approved ones, "approved" only approved ones, "all" also the rejected ones. Screened-out workers never count.

text_samples.description: Latest written answers to show per text question and "Other" box (0 to 50, default 10), each cut to 500 characters. list_submissions has every answer in full.

tools.name: approve_submission
tools.title: Approve submission
tools.description: Approves a submission and pays the worker from the job budget; this cannot be undone. Optional tip $0.01 to $50.00 from the balance, paid to the worker in full. Requires an idempotency_key. Set kind to "survey" for surveys made with create_survey or "ai_task" for AI data-collection tasks; the default "job" covers regular and prefilled jobs.

job_id.description: Id of the job, survey or AI task (job_id from list_jobs or from the create tool).

kind.description: "job" (default) for regular and prefilled jobs, "survey" for surveys made with create_survey, "ai_task" for AI data-collection tasks.

tip.description: Optional tip in USD (0.01 to 50.00) paid from the balance to the worker in full.

idempotency_key.description: A new unique string for this action (e.g. a UUID; letters, digits, _ . : - only, up to 128). Send the same key again only to retry a call that timed out or could not reach the API, so it is never done twice. After an error answer, fix the cause and use a new key: the API replays its stored answer to a reused key.

tools.name: reject_submission
tools.title: Reject submission
tools.description: Rejects a Pending submission; the worker is not paid and sees the reason. Never reject an Approved submission: it has already been paid, and rejecting it does not take the payment back. reason is required and should say exactly what was missing. Requires an idempotency_key. Set kind to "survey" for surveys made with create_survey or "ai_task" for AI data-collection tasks; the default "job" covers regular and prefilled jobs.

job_id.description: Id of the job, survey or AI task (job_id from list_jobs or from the create tool).

kind.description: "job" (default) for regular and prefilled jobs, "survey" for surveys made with create_survey, "ai_task" for AI data-collection tasks.

reason.description: Shown to the worker: exactly what was missing or wrong compared with the instructions.

idempotency_key.description: A new unique string for this action (e.g. a UUID; letters, digits, _ . : - only, up to 128). Send the same key again only to retry a call that timed out or could not reach the API, so it is never done twice. After an error answer, fix the cause and use a new key: the API replays its stored answer to a reused key.

tools.name: approve_all_pending
tools.title: Approve all pending submissions
tools.description: Approves every Pending submission on the job and pays the workers; this cannot be undone. For a survey, only_quality_band "good" approves only the Pending responses in the good quality band and leaves the rest for review. Requires confirm=true and an idempotency_key. Set kind to "survey" for surveys made with create_survey or "ai_task" for AI data-collection tasks; the default "job" covers regular and prefilled jobs.

job_id.description: Id of the job, survey or AI task (job_id from list_jobs or from the create tool).

kind.description: "job" (default) for regular and prefilled jobs, "survey" for surveys made with create_survey, "ai_task" for AI data-collection tasks.

only_quality_band.description: Surveys only: "good" approves only the Pending responses in the good quality band; the ones to check or likely bad stay Pending for review.

confirm.description: Must be true, and only after the user explicitly approved this action and its cost.

idempotency_key.description: A new unique string for this action (e.g. a UUID; letters, digits, _ . : - only, up to 128). Send the same key again only to retry a call that timed out or could not reach the API, so it is never done twice. After an error answer, fix the cause and use a new key: the API replays its stored answer to a reused key.

tools.name: block_worker
tools.title: Block worker
tools.description: Blocks a worker (worker_id from list_submissions of a regular job or a survey) from all of the account's jobs and rejects their pending submissions.

worker_id.description: worker_id of a submission on a regular job or a survey (from list_submissions).

tools.name: unblock_worker
tools.title: Unblock worker
tools.description: Removes a worker from the block list.

tools.name: list_blocked_workers
tools.title: List blocked workers
tools.description: Lists the workers this account has blocked.
